title: An incomplete `cacerts` plug-in CA bundle now stops istiod from starting instead of silently using the self-signed CA

detection.reason: the agent ships a Secret's key NAMES, but a rule cannot express 'a key is MISSING from the set'; the hint names the plug-in CA Secret so the four keys can be checked

quote: With this fix, `istiod` will now validate the entire CA bundle and return an explicit error if any required file is missing, rather than falling back silently.
remediation: istiod 1.27 requires all four files in the `cacerts` Secret (`ca-cert.pem`, `ca-key.pem`, `root-cert.pem`, `cert-chain.pem`) and exits with `failed to create an istiod CA: incomplete signing CA bundle detected` when one is missing — previously only `ca-key.pem` was checked and the rest silently fell back to the self-signed CA. Before upgrading, confirm the Secret carries all four keys; if the mesh has in fact been running on the self-signed CA, either complete the bundle (workloads re-certify on rotation) or delete the partial Secret to keep the self-signed CA deliberately.
verifyCommand: kubectl get secret cacerts -n istio-system -o json | jq -r '.data | keys | join(" ")'  # istiod 1.27 needs all of: ca-cert.pem ca-key.pem root-cert.pem cert-chain.pem — a shorter list stops istiod from starting

title: Istio's bundled Grafana dashboards must be re-imported after upgrading — dashboard UIDs are now fixed

detection.reason: dashboards are files inside Grafana; the Grafana Deployment is the subject

quote: If you use Istio's bundled Grafana dashboards, you'll need to regenerate them after upgrading to get the fixed dashboard linking. Dashboard UIDs are now explicitly defined to enable stable links between dashboards.
remediation: Re-import the 1.27 dashboards (the `istio-grafana-dashboards` ConfigMaps or the upstream JSON) so cross-dashboard links resolve; dashboards imported from an older release keep random UIDs and their links break.
verifyCommand: kubectl get cm -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("istio.*dashboard")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # printed ConfigMaps hold bundled dashboards to regenerate after the 1.27 upgrade

title: The Lightstep and OpenCensus telemetry providers are removed

detection.reason: extension providers live inside the istio ConfigMap's mesh YAML, whose keys the projection keeps and whose contents it does not

quote: The telemetry providers Lightstep and Opencensus are removed in v1.27. Please use the OpenTelemetry provider instead.
remediation: At 1.27 a `lightstep` extension provider silently produces no tracer any more (the config is still accepted, istiod only logs a warning), so tracing through it stops; `opencensus` providers have been inert since 1.23. Replace them with an `opentelemetry` provider (Lightstep/ServiceNow accepts OTLP) and repoint Telemetry resources before upgrading istiod.
verifyCommand: kubectl get cm -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.data.mesh != null) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .data.mesh | split("\n")[] | select(test("lightstep|opencensus")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed line configures a provider 1.27 removes

title: Native sidecars are on by default — `istio-proxy` becomes an init container, which other mutating webhooks and controllers may not expect

detection.reason: which webhooks assume istio-proxy is a regular container is not derivable from their configuration; the mutating webhooks are the population to review

quote: Native sidecars are now enabled by default for eligible pods. This changes `istio-proxy`from a container to an init container. This can cause compatibility issues with other mutating webhooks or controllers in your cluster that expect to modify the `istio-proxy` as a regular container.
remediation: Test every other mutating webhook and any controller that inspects `spec.containers` for `istio-proxy` (vault-injector, OPA/Kyverno mutations, log sidecar injectors, custom operators) against a canary namespace before upgrading; set `ENABLE_NATIVE_SIDECARS=false` on istiod to keep the classic container where a controller cannot be fixed.
verifyCommand: kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("istio") | not) | .metadata.name'  # each printed webhook may mutate pods after Istio injection and must cope with istio-proxy as an init container

title: Three unused multicluster Helm values are dropped from the istiod chart: `global.multiCluster.enabled`, `globalDomainSuffix`, `includeEnvoyFilter`

detection.reason: values are install-time input; only an IstioOperator resource keeps them on the cluster

remediation: No-op: `global.multiCluster.enabled`, `global.multiCluster.globalDomainSuffix` and `global.multiCluster.includeEnvoyFilter` are ignored by the 1.27 chart (istioctl still accepts them). `global.multiCluster.clusterName` and `global.meshID` are unchanged and still required for multicluster.
verifyCommand: kubectl get istiooperators.install.istio.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.values.global.multiCluster.enabled != null or .spec.values.global.multiCluster.globalDomainSuffix != null or .spec.values.global.multiCluster.includeEnvoyFilter != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed IstioOperator sets one of the three values the 1.27 chart ignores
